title: VRoid-lineage anime style profile
description: The de facto 'VRM anime' look as practised by VRoid Studio exports and hand-tuned derivatives: proportions as bone ratios and head counts, a three-tier MToon factor-shading convention (face region never fully shaded under direct light, body/cloth hard two-tone, hair up to a soft two-tone), inverted-hull outlines on surfaces but not on facial features, layered translucent eye materials, spring-bone hair, and a VRoid-typical performance budget. Envelopes are measured from the corpus below and regenerated with `style_lint.py envelopes --write`; fingerprint rules record tool constants and are informational only. pixiv documents the face convention and the gamma-to-linear change for VRoid Studio stable (https://vroid.pixiv.help/hc/en-us/articles/4405597671193): 'shades are weaker at the front and follow the face outline'. This profile is the numerical characterisation of that behaviour.

corpus.note: Local assets measured 2026-09-10 with scripts/style_lint.py. Re-exports of the same VRoid body (AvatarSample_A 0.0/1.0; VRoid_V110_Female, AvatarBlondeRedDress and VRM1_Constraint_Twist_Sample; AvatarSample_V and The President) collapse to effective_n. Two synthetic generator outputs from ../vrm-conformance (smoke_default.vrm, springbone_default.vrm) were used as negative controls and are not in the corpus.

metric_definitions.asset.height_m: max Y of all mesh positions in rest pose minus min(0, bbox min Y). Skinned meshes are taken in bind space (VRM rest == bind).
metric_definitions.proportions.eye_height_ratio: mean world Y of leftEye/rightEye humanoid bones divided by height.
metric_definitions.proportions.ipd_m: distance between leftEye and rightEye bones, metres.
metric_definitions.proportions.arm_span_height_ratio: distance leftHand–rightHand bones / height (hand bones, not fingertips).
metric_definitions.proportions.rest_pose_arm_horizontal_cos: |x component| of the unit vector upperArm→hand in rest pose; 1.0 is a perfect T-pose.
metric_definitions.proportions.limb_asymmetry: max over arm/leg of |left length − right length| / max(left, right).
metric_definitions.proportions.head_height_m: Vertices whose dominant skin joint is head, leftEye, rightEye or jaw, restricted to the centre column |x − head.x| < 15 mm. chin = lowest such vertex with z > head.z (in front of the head bone); crown = highest such vertex. head_height = crown − chin. Includes crown hair and any neck skin weighted to head; does not depend on mesh or material names.
metric_definitions.proportions.eye_height_in_head: (eye bone Y − chin) / head_height_m. 0.5 is the realistic vertical midpoint; anime faces sit lower.
metric_definitions.proportions.head_width_m: X extent of head-dominant vertices within ±10 mm of eye height (includes hair over the temples).
metric_definitions.springs.hair_chains: spring chains whose first joint is a descendant of the head bone.
metric_definitions.springs.head_colliders: colliders attached to the head bone or a descendant.
metric_definitions.expressions.presets: VRM 1.0 preset names present; VRM 0.x presetNames are mapped to their 1.0 equivalents (joy→happy, sorrow→sad, fun→relaxed, a/i/u/e/o→aa/ih/ou/ee/oh).
metric_definitions.material.shadow_end: MToon 1.0 shading = linearstep(−1 + toony, 1 − toony, NdotL + shift). shadow_end = −1 + toony − shift: the NdotL below which the surface is fully in shade colour. −1 means never shaded; 0 means a terminator at grazing light.
metric_definitions.material.lit_start: 1 − toony − shift: NdotL above which the surface is fully lit.
metric_definitions.material.terminator_width: lit_start − shadow_end = 2(1 − toony). 0 is a hard two-tone edge; 2 is a full Lambert gradient.
metric_definitions.material.shade_luminance_ratio: Rec.709 luminance of shadeColorFactor / luminance of baseColorFactor (textures not sampled).
metric_definitions.material.shade_warmth: (shade.r/shade.g) / (base.r/base.g); > 1 means the shade colour is redder than the base.
metric_definitions.material.outline_width_m: outlineWidthFactor when outlineWidthMode == worldCoordinates, else null. VRM 0.x _OutlineWidth (cm) is converted ×0.01.
metric_definitions.material.*: VRM 0.x MToon properties are converted to 1.0 space following three-vrm's VRMMaterialsV0CompatPlugin: colour factors (_Color rgb, _ShadeColor, _EmissionColor, _RimColor, _OutlineColor) are sRGB-decoded to linear because 0.x stores gamma-space colours and 1.0 stores linear (exact sRGB EOTF as in UniVRM and VRoid's exporter; three-vrm approximates with pow 2.2); shadingToony = lerp(_ShadeToony, 1, 0.5 + 0.5·_ShadeShift); shadingShift = −_ShadeShift − (1 − shadingToony); giEqualization = 1 − _IndirectLightIntensity; transparent render queues map in order to offsets −9…0; _UvAnimScrollY flips sign. Shading-shift textures, shade textures, normals and renderer shadowing are not sampled: every shading metric here is a factor-only, direct-light statement.
metric_definitions.mtoon_defaults: Absent MToon 1.0 fields take the schema defaults (VRMC_materials_mtoon.schema.json): shadeColorFactor [1,1,1], shadingToony 0.9, shadingShift 0, giEqualization 0.9, rim fresnel 5, rim lift 0, rimLightingMix 1. The MToon prose describes a black default shade colour while the schema says white; the linter follows the schema. VRoid always writes the field, so the corpus is unaffected.

vrchat_avatar_performance_ranks.note: Cited for context only. VRChat ranks are computed by its SDK on the imported Unity asset (compressed texture memory, PhysBone components), which none of the metrics here reproduce; the corpus' 77k-triangle maximum already exceeds the PC 'Poor' triangle ceiling. The budget rules below encode the VRoid-typical envelope, not VRChat ranks.

rules.title: Eyes sit in the top sixth of the figure
Long legs: leg root above mid-height
4.5–8 heads tall
rules.rationale: Realistic adults measure ~7.5–8 heads with a bare skull; this metric includes crown hair so anime figures land lower. Chibi (2–4 heads) is a different profile. VRM 0.x models face −Z, VRM 1.0 models face +Z; the chin search uses the version's forward axis.

rules.title: Eyes below the head's vertical midpoint
rules.rationale: Large-eye anime construction places the eye line at roughly 35–40% of chin-to-crown; realistic construction places it at 50%.

rules.title: Head bone near the jaw line

provenance.note: VRMC_vrm humanoid requires T-pose rest; retargeting in VRMAnimationLoader assumes it.

rules.title: Face region is never fully in shade for front-facing light
rules.rationale: The headline anime rule: no nose or brow shadows. VRoid's 'toon' preset does it with shift +0.71 (fully lit above NdotL −0.62); its 'soft' preset with toony 0.05 (gradient spanning the whole hemisphere). Both leave the fully-shaded region behind the head.

provenance.note: 18/21 face_skin materials conform; PompaGirl, AnnieV0 and pixiv's constraint sample use plain toon faces.

rules.title: Body and clothing use a hard two-tone terminator
rules.rationale: toony ≥ 0.8. The soft-gradient VRoid preset (toony 0.2, width 1.6) is a recognised minority style and fails this rule by design.

provenance.note: 19/21 body_skin materials conform; the soft-gradient minority is AvatarSample_A/B-era exports, Mike Scott and Vita.

rules.title: Body shade begins at or behind grazing light
Hair terminator width up to 1.4 (not full Lambert)
rules.rationale: Hair is allowed a softer terminator than body (VRoid default 0.4 vs 0.1) but this rule does not require it to be softer; hard-edged hair also conforms.

rules.title: Hair shade begins near grazing light
Skin shade colour is warmer (redder) than the base
Cloth and hair shade luminance ≥ 25% of base
Parametric rim is off or subtle
Skin and cloth are not emissive

provenance.note: hair emissive is used deliberately (28/60 hair materials) and is not constrained.

rules.title: Every material has a role
rules.rationale: Material-scoped rules only see materials with a role. An unclassified material is silently exempt, so the report must say so; pass --roles to assign roles by name.

rules.title: Skin and cloth carry a world-space inverted-hull outline

provenance.note: accessories (cat ears, tails, glasses) are excluded; 5 of them ship without an outline.

rules.title: Eyes, brows, lashes and mouth have no outline
Body, cloth and hair are cutout or opaque, never blended
Iris, highlight, eyeline, lash and brow are alpha-blended layers
Facial layers draw at or before the default queue

provenance.note: VRoid orders eyeline/iris −4…−1 under the highlight; the face skin stays at 0.

rules.title: Iris, sclera and mouth are single-sided
At least three spring-bone hair chains rooted under the head

provenance.note: PompaGirl (a hand-tuned VRM 0.x asset) has no spring chains rooted under the head and no head collider.
See project memory on VMK#324/#326: authored gravityPower is applied at spec scale, never substituted.

rules.title: A head collider keeps hair off the face
Five visemes, blink and four emotions are authored
rules.rationale: A profile requirement, not a specification one: VRMC_vrm expressions.md states that all preset expressions are optional. Lip-sync, blinking and emotion drivers in this style assume these ten exist.

provenance.note: surprised has no VRM 0.x equivalent, so it is a separate 1.0-only rule.

rules.title: surprised authored (VRM 1.0 preset with no 0.x equivalent)

provenance.note: VRMMetalKit's morph kernel caps active targets at 8 per dispatch; authored count only bounds memory.

rules.title: Eye offset 2–12 cm above the head bone
VRM 1.0 meta points at the VRM Public License
VRM 0.x licenseName is a valid enum
VRM 0.x allowedUserName is a valid enum
VRM 0.x commercialUssageName is a valid enum

provenance.note: Distinct POSITION accessors; asset.vertex_references sums per-primitive counts and is 2–15× larger on VRoid exports because primitives share one accessor.

rules.title: VRoid Studio exports exactly Face/Body/Hair skinned meshes
VRoid Studio 1.x face carries 57 morph targets
VRoid sets rim fresnel power 100 and lift 0.1 (rim effectively off)

provenance.note: The 0.x value (0.2745, 0.0902, 0.1255) sRGB-decodes to the same linear colour the 1.0 exporter writes, so both generations agree once colour space is normalised.
